nodes.label: Single-user self-hosted threat model
nodes.rationale: supermux is a single-user, self-hosted broker driving local agent CLIs; the machine it runs on is treated as trusted, which is why the security boundary sits at the network edge (front auth) rather than inside the host.

nodes.label: HttpOnly cmux_token device cookie
nodes.rationale: All browser access is gated by the cookie; requests without it get 401. Delivered HttpOnly so it is never readable from JavaScript. Mutating requests additionally require a same-origin Origin header as CSRF defense-in-depth on top of SameSite=Lax.

nodes.label: Device token storage and comparison
nodes.rationale: Tokens are random, stored only as SHA-256 hashes, compared in constant time, and rate-limited on failure — defeating both database disclosure and timing/brute-force attacks.

nodes.label: /internal/agent-hook/* per-boot secret gate
nodes.rationale: Local agent hooks only; gated by a per-boot secret embedded in the hook URLs and explicitly not part of the public API.

nodes.label: Public (opt-in) reverse-proxied dev servers
nodes.rationale: Exposed ports default to the same device cookie (Domain=.<base>); marking a subdomain public skips broker auth entirely, so it must be treated exactly like exposing a port on the internet.

nodes.label: Secrets at rest (~/.mux/state/.env, push-keys.json)
nodes.rationale: Telegram/provider API keys and the VAPID private key live on disk at mode 0600 and must never be committed.
